levels.title: Money foundations
levels.summary: Where your money goes, why a cash cushion comes first, and how debt interest works.

modules.title: Where your money goes
modules.summary: The basic map of your money.

lessons.title: What a budget is actually for
objectives: Explain a budget as a plan for your money, not a punishment
List the three buckets most budgets use
key_points: A budget is a plan you make before the month starts
Most budgets split money into needs, wants and future you
A plan you can keep beats a perfect plan you quit

try_it.prompt: Write down your monthly take-home pay and your three biggest costs.

quiz.q: What is a budget mainly for?
choices: Planning where your money goes before you spend it
quiz.why: A budget is a plan made ahead of time.
Future you covers saving and paying down debt.

lessons.title: Why a cash cushion comes first
objectives: Explain what an emergency cushion is for
Explain why money you need soon shouldn't be in the stock market
key_points: A cushion covers surprises so they don't become debt
Money you may need soon has no time to recover from a drop
Start small: even one month of costs helps

try_it.prompt: Add up one month of must-pay costs. That's your first cushion target.

quiz.q: What is an emergency cushion for?
quiz.why: It keeps surprises from turning into debt.

quiz.q: Why keep it out of the stock market?
choices: You may need it right when prices are down
quiz.why: Short-term money has no time to recover from a drop.

levels.title: Your first investments
levels.summary: Compound growth, risk, and what an index fund actually is.

modules.title: How growth and risk work
modules.summary: Why time matters, and why prices swing.

lessons.title: Compound growth, explained with $100 a month
objectives: Explain compound growth in plain words
key_points: Growth can earn growth of its own over time
Starting earlier gives money more years to grow
Growth is never promised: investments can lose value
lessons.risk_note: Examples are hypothetical. Investments can fall in value, including the money you put in.

try_it.prompt: Compare starting at your age with starting 5 years later.

choices: Your gains can earn gains of their own
Your bank pays a fixed bonus
Early money gets more years to grow
Taxes are lower for young people
quiz.why: Time is the input you control most.

quiz.q: Which is true about investment growth?
choices: It only happens in savings accounts
quiz.why: No investment is free of risk.
